title: Morphology of ceramic regulates the deposition behavior and mechanical properties of cold spray additive manufactured Al2O3/2024 aluminum matrix composites
InformationInFigures: Yes. Tensile specimen dimensions (Fig.3). Particle size distribution (Fig.1), Porosity values (Fig.9) Particle impact velocities (Fig. 15). data extracted with PlotDigitizer. Stress strain curves (Fig. 20)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: 2024 Al: near-spherical; Al2O3: complex carbon-60–like spherical aggregates
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: the Al2O3 has a similar D50 value at 35 μm
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Heat_Treatment_Description: dried in a furnace at 80°C for 30 min

experimentalProperties.Spraying_System_Model: Custom cold spray system, Northwestern Polytechnical University
experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: The surface layer with residual stresses was removed with vibration polishing for 4 h.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: significantly more ceramic deposited compared even with 50 vol% of spherical Al2O3 powder sample, therefore much higher deposition efficiency due to irregular shape of Al2O3. porosity is low and ceramic particles re-embedded in the matrix. pores found in between and inside large ceramic particles. deposit ceramic content is 3.3 vol% higher than in the feedstock powder. The deformation structure is non-uniform and consists of fine equiaxed grains and a few deformed ‘pancake’ grains. The equiaxed grains descend from the feed stock, while the deformed pancake grains are produced during impact. In addition to those two types of grains, a small number of fine grains are present. particles undergo dynamic recrystallization. observed dimples.

Experiments.Notes: 10% irregular particles. The particle impact velocity was calculated with a simulation and statistical analysis (ANSYS-FLUENT 2020 R1 software for 3D finite volume analysis), and I reported it as a range since alumina and Al particles had distinct velocities. The lower value is Al
